interface_revision: 4.3.0: redesigned interface (progress rail, approach cards, review-gated generation); unused files removed; matplotlib dependency dropped. Scientific core files unchanged (hashes above). 4.4.0: AI-only generation, readable variable names, parallel batches.
ai_batching: Default 25 participants per request; four requests per 100-person dataset run in parallel. SPA_BATCH_SIZE=100 restores the single-request protocol of the original MIDUS evaluation.
public_variable_names: MIDUS source codes never leave the server; all pages, API responses and downloads use readable names (spa/public.py). Verified by automated scan of every response and by browser QA of all visible text and downloads.
free_numerical_demo: Removed in 4.4.0; every simulation uses AI generation.
approach_numbering: SPA1-SPA8 as in the revised proposal throughout code, run names, uploads and outputs: SPA7 demographic-only profiles; SPA8 demographic and psychological profiles. Prompt bank, study configuration and verified original-study files are byte-identical to the original; spa/numbering.py relabels them on load. Changed core files (spa/analysis.py, spa/study.py, spa/workflow.py, spa/prompts.py) contain numbering and label changes only; statistical code (metrics.py) is unchanged.
upload_templates: SPA4 takes target proportions, one row per demographic category (variable, category, category_label, lower and upper for age bands, proportion), with no participant data. SPA5 and SPA6 take exactly 50 pilot participants. SPA7 and SPA8 take at least 100 participant profiles, one row per participant and one column per variable.
signature_fix: 4.5.0: signed input fingerprints normalise whole-number decimals so uploads survive browser JSON serialisation (previously a 3.0 sent back as 3 caused submission to be rejected).
wording_revision_4_6_1: User-facing text in spa/study.py and spa/workflow.py was reworded (message strings only, no logic changes); their hashes above are updated. Study configuration, prompt bank and model-facing prompt text are unchanged.
spa4_revision_4_6_2: SPA4 input restored to target proportions as in version 4.2.0. spa/workflow.py changed in its SPA4 input handling and wording only; the quota construction (profiles_from_proportions) and prompt bank are unchanged. The example proportions are fictional.
interface_5_0: Goal-first flow following the proposal: research goal (Goal 1 scores, Goal 2 relationships), then research stage, then the Table 6 recommendation; study chosen once on Study and data (MIDUS demonstration uses example inputs automatically; own study uploads only what the approach needs); custom demographics optional except for SPA4, SPA7 and SPA8; the word fidelity removed from the interface.
interface_5_1: Guided yes/no questions about the research stage lead to one Table 6 recommendation, with alternatives collapsed; the MIDUS demonstration always uses the supplied example inputs (viewable, never replaced); custom studies need only a title (target population removed; SPA3 asks who the participants are); a fictional MIDUS reference supports practising the comparison step; changing the study keeps the chosen approach.
interface_6_0: Design B research console: top status bar, side navigation with step statuses, separate pages for the seven steps and reference material, inspector with selections, evidence and activity log, results table of all eight approaches on the approach page; the proposal's two goals (Goal 2 merged); messages stick below the top bar with Dismiss; IBM Plex Sans self-hosted under the SIL Open Font License.
interface_6_1: Study-first flow after the supplied revised design: 1 Choose your study, 2 Research goal, 3 Questionnaire (own study), 4 Your situation, 5 Approach, 6 Inputs (own study), 7 Check and generate, 8 Datasets. The MIDUS demonstration skips steps 3 and 6 and shows its example inputs on Check and generate. Later steps stay locked until earlier ones are complete, and changing the study, goal, situation or approach asks for the approach to be confirmed again. Compare with human data is removed from the interface and the API (/api/compare, the fictional MIDUS reference and the custom comparison). Overview content and the Errors and help page are kept.
